drivingQuestion: What determines whether a practice is forbidden as one of the ways of the Amorite?
outcomeNote: A criterion is stated in explanation of the mishna; it is challenged only in the following unit.

segments.he: וְאֵין קוֹבְרִים אוֹתָהּ. אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רְפוּאָה – אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם דַּרְכֵי הָאֱמוֹרִי, אֵין בּוֹ רְפוּאָה – יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם דַּרְכֵי הָאֱמוֹרִי.
segments.en: § The mishna adds: «But one may neither bury it» at an intersection, nor may one hang it on a tree, due to the prohibition against following the ways of the Amorite. The Gemara cites «Abaye and Rava, who both said: Anything that has» an apparently effective «medicinal» purpose or any other logical reason behind it «is not subject to» the prohibition against following «the ways of the Amorite.» But if «it does not have» an apparently effective «medicinal» purpose «it is subject to» the prohibition against following «the ways of the Amorite.»

moves.summary: quotes the mishna's ban on burying the placenta at a crossroads
moves.about: the mishna's clause forbidding one to bury the placenta at a crossroads or hang it on a tree

moves.summary: Abaye and Rava jointly lay down the criterion: what has a medicinal purpose is not darkhei ha-Emori
moves.about: both hold that what has a medicinal purpose is not subject to the prohibition of the ways of the Amorite

edges.cueHe: כל דבר שיש בו רפואה – אין בו משום דרכי האמורי
edges.about: what makes a practice fall under the ways of the Amorite — the absence of a medicinal purpose, which is why burying the placenta at a crossroads is forbidden
edges.proposedPredicate: interpret.supplies_reason_for — «כל דבר שיש בו רפואה» — supplies the operative rationale of a cited prohibition in place of the reason one would assume; interprets covers saying what words mean, not what makes a rule apply
